title: Is Your Red The Same as My Red?
beats: Shows three colors everyone agrees on, then flips: color is made in the head, not the world
Wavelength is measurable; the experience of it is not
You and I both say red for a strawberry; how would we ever know our inner experiences match
Color blindness is detectable because failures show on tests; invisible differences would not be
Maybe differences exist but behave identically on every test; notes preferences for colors might already hint at this
Alien who can never feel pain learns all the biology but never the feeling
Names the idea afterward: qualia and the Explanatory Gap
Tommy Edison, blind since birth, says hot-red and cold-blue explanations never made him see color
Dennett: privacy may be a limit of language, not in principle; a future language might transmit color
Admits no answer for now; reframes being able to ask as the remarkable part
Pivot: apes sign, use tools, feel things, yet none has ever asked a question
Theory of Mind named as the explanation
Sally-Anne cookie story told step by step; child under 4 predicts the wrong box
Apes not asking is the same error as the child: others' minds are not seen as separate
Chocolate, red: we are alone in our minds, but we can ask. Stay curious

metrics.misconception: partial: opens by stating color is not out there, undercutting the assumption that seeing is shared
metrics.examples: 4 (alien and pain, Tommy Edison, signing apes, Sally-Anne); unrelated in domain, linked by minds-are-separate
metrics.ending: Callback to the red question, answered with ask and stay curious rather than a fact

principles.1: confirmed: strawberry, chocolate, color words everyone already uses (0:51, 8:40)
principles.2: confirmed: only three terms introduced, each after its concept: qualia 2:57, Explanatory Gap 3:13, Theory of Mind 6:50
principles.4: partly: alien-with-no-pain analogy at 2:03, but the topic is philosophical so no rigor step follows
principles.5: confirmed: Sally-Anne acted out as a literal story at 7:12
principles.7: partly: viewer is invited to predict where Sally looks, but the answer is given quickly (7:47)
principles.8: partly: topic shifts at 5:27 are fast with no slowdown; the density is carried by stacked examples rather than slower speech
principles.9: partly: same structure (you cannot see inside another mind) repeated across alien, blind man, ape, child
principles.11: confirmed: color is internal, then differences undetectable, then ineffability, then name, then other minds
principles.12: confirmed: Tommy Edison, Dennett, Jordania paper, Sally-Anne, Hutson-style outside sources pulled in
principles.13: partly: plain tone throughout and expert names used, but tool choices are not explained

new_moves.name: unanswerable-answer
new_moves.what: Admits the question cannot be answered and reframes the ability to ask as the payoff

new_moves.name: tangent-as-mirror
new_moves.what: Apparent detour (apes, Sally-Anne) returns to the hook as the same structural error

theory: The video treats the learner as the experiment: the central idea (other minds are inaccessible) is shown through four different cases rather than defined, and the vocabulary arrives only after the idea is felt. The ending turns an unanswerable question into the lesson itself.
velocity: For open questions, add an honest-caveat beat type to the orchestrator and let the tutor end on a reframe rather than force an answer
Scene builder: reuse one structural pattern across several cases and have the learner predict before the reveal (Sally-Anne style)
Learner model: delay jargon until the learner has used the idea in their own words
quote: I can never know if my red looks the same as your red.
